gaps.title: Source-player total duration rounds 150.01 seconds up to 02:31
gaps.claim: The AI Video Enhance source-player time readout displays the ceiling of the imported video's total duration after the slash; 150.01 seconds displays 00:00/02:31 rather than 00:00/02:30 at the initial position.
gaps.decision: not from the spec: Total duration after the slash is rounded up (150.01 s → 02:31): user requirement 2026-10-21; our spec draws 「00:00/12:30」 with no rounding rule.

gaps.title: Source within active Mode cap fills one filmstrip viewport
gaps.claim: When source duration is no longer than the active Mode maximum, the entire bottom filmstrip fills one
gaps.decision: stated differently: Same source (PM 9/29 ⑥, which they quote): 「the strip scale depends only on the video length; switching Mode does not re-lay the strip」. Their case makes one viewport = the active Mode limit (150 s in Professional) and re-scales on a Mode switch; ours follows the ⑥ text (TC-045). Neither is newer: ask PM which is meant.

gaps.title: Mode info displays Standard: Great quality · up to 8 min and
gaps.claim: Mode info displays: Standard: up to 8 minutes. Professional: up to 2m 30s.
gaps.decision: older spec: Their pass text uses PM 9/29 「Standard: up to 8 minutes. Professional: up to 2m 30s.」 (their own title quotes the Design); the Design bubble 「Standard: Great quality · up to 8 min」 / 「Professional: Maximum detail · up to 2:30」 is newer (TC-035).

gaps.title: Task objects are retained in cloud storage for one year.
gaps.claim: Task objects are retained in cloud storage for one year.
gaps.decision: not covered: Not covered on purpose: the one-year cloud retention is stated (Recent notice) but we marked it NOT TESTABLE (R-117, needs a year); TC-140 checks only the notice.

gaps.title: Import source 2160p: verify 2K+ source is rejected before settings
gaps.claim: AI Video Enhance rejects importing every source classified by the active specification as 2K or higher before opening the settings flow, regardless of orientation, container or codec, fps, or duration; the source is not loaded and no Enhance task starts.
gaps.decision: stated differently: Theirs (user requirement 2026-10-16) rejects any 2K-or-higher source before the panel opens; our spec (Design lookup 1081p+ → 4K, PM E1 「≤ 4K」) lets 1440p and 4K sources open with 4K selected (TC-058) and rejects only sources over 4K (TC-022). Their rule is newer but not in our spec set: confirm with PM (our Q-13).

gaps.title: During-drag endpoint preview: left handle earlier
gaps.claim: During left-handle dragging, Preview displays the frame at the dragged endpoint.
gaps.decision: not covered: Not covered: our spec says either side handle can be dragged (PM B1 [Design], Design 「Length」 frames) and every row drags only the right handle (TC-042, TC-044, TC-074). No row drags the left handle.

gaps.title: Generate combination: Standard / Natural / 60fps / 720p
gaps.claim: Every Mode / Enhancement style / fps / Resolution combination supported by the release can complete enhancement and produce its corresponding playable result. · An eligible user with sufficient credits can start enhancement directly. · A generating task is shown in Recent Task with a processing state. · A completed task offers View. · Tapping View on a completed task opens its Result page. · Play on Result starts visible playback of the completed generated video. · Save Result stores the generated video on the phone as a separate file. · The saved generated video uses the selected supported output fps. · The saved generated video uses the selected supported output Resolution. · Every enhancement configuration consumes credits. · For every current SPEC-supported Mode/style/fps/Resolution combination, elapsed time from the first observed remaining-time display in Recent Task to the declared same-task completion signal is1.5–2.5 times actual selected video duration.
gaps.decision: not covered: Not covered: no row generates with a non-default setting. Our only generation (TC-110 → TC-143) uses the defaults; the Mode, Enhancement style, fps and Resolution chips are variants of the rule and pass 10 would give each value its own generation (about six rows: Professional, Sharp, 60fps, 120fps, 720p, 4K), not their 36-way product.

Our only generation (TC-110 → TC-143) uses the defaults; the Mode, Enhancement style, fps and Resolution chips are variants of the rule and pass 10 would give each value its own generation (about six rows: Professional, Sharp, 60fps, 120fps, 720p, 4K), not their 36-way product.

gaps.title: Professional rejects any Standard selection over 150s (151s boundary)
gaps.claim: Professional retains its normal selectable appearance when Standard selection exceeds 2:30. · Tapping Professional with a selection longer than 2:30 displays: Professional mode supports up to 2m 30s. Shorten your selection to switch. · Tapping Professional with a selection longer than 2:30 leaves Standard selected. · A rejected Professional switch preserves the entire selected interval: start, end and length; it never automatically shortens or moves the selection.
gaps.decision: older spec: Behaviour is ours too (TC-071, TC-073: blocked, Mode stays, chip looks normal). Only the toast copy differs: theirs is PM 9/29 「Professional mode supports up to 2m 30s. Shorten your selection to switch.」; the newer Design frame 「Mode 長度上限」 (Design 26.09 v2, 1005; none of its copy is in their 10/07 PDF) says 「Professional supports clips up to 2:30. Shorten your selection to switch.」.

gaps.title: Long-source filmstrip 481s: Mode-specific 480s / 150s viewport
gaps.claim: When source duration exceeds the active Mode maximum, the filmstrip scrolls horizontally and one viewport represents that Mode maximum: 480 seconds in Standard or 150 seconds in Professional. · Switching Standard / Professional recalculates filmstrip scale from the active Mode maximum. For a source longer than 150 seconds, the visible filmstrip proportion and handle screen positions are expected to change; chronological thumbnail order and any selection valid in both Modes keep the same start, end and duration.
gaps.decision: stated differently: Same source (PM 9/29 ⑥, which they quote): 「the strip scale depends only on the video length; switching Mode does not re-lay the strip」. Their case makes one viewport = the active Mode limit (150 s in Professional) and re-scales on a Mode switch; ours follows the ⑥ text (TC-045). Neither is newer: ask PM which is meant.
